bibliographic.title: Generative AI in Medicine and Healthcare: A Comprehensive Review of Foundational Technologies, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives
bibliographic.authors: Tomoshige Nakamura, Wataru Uchida, Akira Yamamoto, Shigeki Aoki
bibliographic.citation_apa: Nakamura, T., Uchida, W., Yamamoto, A., & Aoki, S. (2026). Generative AI in medicine and healthcare: A comprehensive review of foundational technologies, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Juntendo Medical Journal. https://doi.org/10.14789/ejmj.JMJ25-0036-R

methodology.sample_description: Peer-reviewed articles and high-impact preprints or conference papers on generative AI, LLMs, diffusion models, NeRF/3DGS, medical imaging, clinical documentation, and drug discovery retrieved from PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and arXiv through May 2025
methodology.technology_context: Transformers and LLMs, diffusion models, NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting, RAG, on-premises LLMs, no-code platforms, clinical documentation automation, medical imaging, drug discovery, surgical simulation

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed healthcare review that explicitly covers LLMs, RAG, data security, and a robust governance framework including bias, interpretability, and accountability in a regulated medical context. However, the provided text centers on foundational technologies and broad clinical applications rather than conversational systems, chatbots, dialogue governance, observability, audit logs, human handoff, or contestability specific to conversational AI.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial methods text were supplied; metadata venue conflicts with the PDF (IEEE Xplore vs Juntendo Medical Journal), and conversational-governance fit cannot be fully verified without the complete full text.

appraisal.notes: The review states a clear objective and describes databases, keywords, and prioritization criteria, but the excerpt does not report a full systematic review protocol, screening flow, included-study count, quality appraisal of primary studies, or explicit limitations section.

cerqual.explanation: Findings about healthcare LLM deployment, RAG, security, and governance are coherent and adequately supported in the available text, but confidence is moderated by incomplete full-text access and limited direct coverage of conversational governance mechanisms.

coding.theme: Generative AI deployment and governance in healthcare
rq_alignment: weak alignment with conversational AI oversight

synthesis.main_claim: Generative AI, especially LLMs together with diffusion models and 3D synthesis technologies, can transform medicine and healthcare, but real-world integration requires technical safeguards such as RAG and on-premises deployment plus a robust governance framework addressing bias, interpretability, and accountability.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured healthcare-focused review linking foundational generative AI technologies to clinical use cases and system-level implementation issues, including hallucination mitigation, data security, and ethical-legal governance.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for healthcare LLM governance, RAG-based risk mitigation, security-conscious deployment, and accountability themes; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance, dialogue oversight, logging/tracing, or contestability unless later sections add that content.
